title: Reserved pool admission deadband drift causing silent request rejects
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A subset of tenants experienced silent request rejects (504-style client errors surfaced as throttling) during high-burst windows when reserved pool admission logic applied a drifted deadband; autoscaler failed to admit burst slots quickly enough. This caused escalations from two enterprise customers using Dedicated reserved pools and resulted in degraded throughput for some latency-sensitive workloads.

What happened: During a rollout of a heuristic change to admission deadband tuning (merged in runtime-1.25), a miscalibrated decay factor for recent-headroom measurements caused the admission window to shrink progressively under sustained but spiky load. The admission controller began rejecting admission requests that should have been allowed given actual headroom, because the deadband counter undercounted free slots. Rejections were visible as admission denies and increased tail latencies due to fallback routing.

Scope: Affected tenants were primarily medium-large dedicated customers with burst-enabled pools in us-west-2. Roughly 4 tenants showed repeated incident signatures over a 6-hour window with peak request denials of ~18% above baseline.

Immediate impact: Customer-initiated escalations to SRE/SE teams and Pager rotations. Temporary mitigation was required to restore acceptable service levels while we prepared a patch and coordinated customer communications.

Root cause: The new deadband decay used integer-based epoch compaction which lost precision when headroom oscillated near small values. Combined with a mis-specified backoff multiplier in admissionPath.go (factor of 0.6 instead of 0.9), the computed effective headroom trended low causing admission to reject safe bursts. Two code regressions surfaced together: the decay precision loss and the multiplier typo.

Fix deployed: 1) Hotpatch: Reverted the decay change to the previous floating-point algorithm and corrected the multiplier to 0.9. 2) Added guardrail to admission controller to compare admission decisions against a short empirical sampling of actual slot allocation success (5s window) to avoid persistent mis-rejects. 3) Patch rolled as runtime-1.25.1 and propagated to Dedicated control-plane and edge admission services.

Verification: Post-deploy telemetry shows admission reject rate returned to baseline within 12 minutes of rollout and customer SLA error rates dropped to normal in all reported tenants. Canary and canary-2 regions observed no regressions in successful admission under equivalent synthetic traffic.

Permanent work: - Replace integer compaction math with unit-tested decimal arithmetic and add fuzz tests. - Add long-tail admission diagnostic metrics (per-tenant sampled admission probability) to Console. - Tighten CI gate: simulated burst workload test that asserts <2% additional reject rate compared to baseline. - Evaluate switching admission heuristic to a predictive headroom estimator (experiment tracked in dedicated-autoscaler-improvements).
